title: Reschedule Meetings for Maximum Free Time II
summary: Given an event duration eventTime and two integer arrays startTime and endTime each of length n, representing the start and end times of n non-overlapping meetings within the event, you can reschedule at most one meeting by adjusting its start time while keeping the duration the same, to ensure all meetings remain non-overlapping.
statement: Given an event duration eventTime and two integer arrays startTime and endTime each of length n, representing the start and end times of n non-overlapping meetings within the event, you can reschedule at most one meeting by adjusting its start time while keeping the duration the same, to ensure all meetings remain non-overlapping. The goal is to maximize the longest continuous period of free time during the event. Return the maximum amount of free time possible after rescheduling at most one meeting. Note that meetings cannot be rescheduled to times outside the event duration and must remain non-overlapping. The rescheduled meeting's order can change.
constraints: Meetings are positive-duration, sorted, non-overlapping, and contained in 0..event_time.
Move at most one meeting, keeping its duration; unlike the ordered version, its position in the sequence may change.
Return the longest continuous free interval possible.
hints: Removing a meeting always joins its two adjacent gaps; relocating it elsewhere also frees its own duration when another gap can hold it.
Precompute the largest gap strictly before and after each meeting’s adjacent gaps.
For each meeting compare the joined gaps alone with joined gaps plus duration when an outside gap is large enough.
Only outside gaps may host the meeting without splitting the candidate joined interval, and prefix/suffix maxima test exactly those locations.
editorial: Only outside gaps may host the meeting without splitting the candidate joined interval, and prefix/suffix maxima test exactly those locations.
